title: The Analytics Engine uses luxon DateTime everywhere because a JS Date cannot report whether it was constructed in UTC
content:
This is one of the few places the Powerhouse docs record the reasoning behind an API choice rather than just the choice.

The team started with the built-in `Date`. The problem is not that `Date` cannot represent UTC — `new Date('2024-12-25T14:46:22.001Z')` parses UTC fine — it is that the resulting object is a local-time object with **no way to ask whether it was constructed from a UTC timestamp**. You can call the constructor and end up with a different instant than the one you thought you passed in, and nothing in the type or the object tells you. `toISO()` will happily emit a UTC string either way.

Strings were considered and rejected: they carry their own class of problems and are only checkable at runtime.

luxon's `DateTime` carries time, date, and timezone in one object, and the docs' summary of why it won is characteristically blunt: it is "difficult (but not impossible) to create a luxon `DateTime` object with a timezone you weren't intending to use." For a time-series analytics system, where a silent timezone shift moves numbers into the wrong bucket rather than producing an error, that difficulty is the feature.

The consequence is that luxon appears on both sides of the API: `AnalyticsSeriesInput.start`/`end` and `AnalyticsQuery.start`/`end` are `DateTime`, and `GroupedPeriodResult.start`/`end` come back as `DateTime`. Series insertion in the shipped processors uses `DateTime.fromISO(operation.timestampUtcMs)`, so the operation log's own UTC timestamp is the input rather than any local clock reading — which also keeps analytics writes deterministic under replay.

Provenance: draft `03-Build/04-WorkWithData/_06-Analytics Engine/typescript/index.md` ("A note about times"); luxon imports confirmed across `packages/analytics-engine/{core,browser,knex}/src/` and `packages/shared/processors/drive-analytics/` at 6.2.2-dev.45.
description: Series bounds and query windows are luxon DateTime objects. The stated design goal is making a timezone mistake hard to make silently in a time-series system.
